texto: With an infinitive, **reprocher à quelqu'un de**: **Je te reproche de venir en retard** is used. There is also **reprocher à quelqu'un que** + subjunctive: **Je lui reproche qu'il ne soit pas venu** (I reproach you that you have not come).
**Reconnaître** (recognize) goes with **que** or with infinitive: **Je reconnais avoir tort** (I recognize that I am wrong).
**Je reconnais que j'ai tort** makes the same sense.

filas: Je te reproche de venir en retard.
Je lui reproche qu'il ne soit pas venu.
Je te pardonne de ne pas venir.

frases.fr: Je te reproche de venir en retard.
frases.en: I reproach you for being late.

frases.fr: Tu as raison, je reconnais avoir tort.
frases.en: You're right, I recognize being wrong.

frases.fr: Je te pardonne, mais ne recommence pas !
frases.es: Te perdono, ¡pero no vuelvas a hacerlo!
frases.en: I forgive you, but don't do it again!
analisis: Don't start again, don't repeat it.

frases.en: Promise, I won't do it again.
analisis: I won't start again, I won't repeat it (simple futur)

bloques.pregunta: How do you say «I reproach you for being late.»?

opciones.texto: Je te reproche de venir en retard.
opciones.explicacion: «Reprocher à quelqu'un de» + infinitive.

opciones.texto: Je te reproche que tu viens en retard.
opciones.explicacion: After «reprocher que», the subordinate must require subjunctive.

opciones.texto: Je te reproche venir en retard.
opciones.explicacion: The «de» preposition is missing in front of the infinitive.

bloques.pregunta: What construction does «reprocher» use with infinitive?

opciones.explicacion: Dativa (IOC) + «de» + infinitive preposition.
«que» requires subjunctive, never indicative mode.
The «à» prepositional mark of the person complement is missing.

bloques.frase: Je te ___ de venir en retard.

opciones.explicacion: First person of singular of the verb «reprocher».
It means «reconozco» and does not fit «je te... de venir».
It means «admito» and does not govern this structure with second-person pronoun.
First person from the present «reconnaître» («reconnaître avoir tort»).
It means «reprocho» and it doesn't make any direct reflexive sense here.
It means «recomienzo» and does not rule infinitive composed of error.

bloques.frase: Je te reproche de venir en retard.

opciones.texto: I reproach you for being late.
opciones.explicacion: Precise translation of «reprocher à quelqu'un de» + infinitive.

opciones.texto: I reproach you for coming late.
opciones.explicacion: It modifies the infinitive structure by an inadequate indication.

opciones.texto: I'm asking you to be late.
opciones.explicacion: Confusion the reproach with a request («demander de»).

bloques.audio: Je te pardonne, mais ne recommence pas !

opciones.texto: I forgive you, but don't do it again!
opciones.explicacion: «Pardonner» = forgive; «ne recommence pas» = negative imperative.

opciones.texto: I don't forgive you, start over!
opciones.explicacion: It inverts the affirmative value of forgiveness and the negative value of the imperative.

opciones.texto: I forgive you and recommend calm.
opciones.explicacion: Confusion «recommencer» with «recommander».

bloques.explicacion: Madness that means admitting one's own fault.

bloques.pregunta: What prepositional regime does the verb «reprocher» follow when followed by an infinitive?

opciones.explicacion: «de» is used against the subordinate infinitive: «Je te reproche de venir en retard».
The «à» preposition introduces the person (IOC), not the dependent infinitive.
«Pour» is not used with infinitive in the standard «reprocher» regimen.

intro: Today, the advanced indirect discourse: not only do we say what someone said, but how he said it (reproach, admit, insinuate, scream).
